holidays.name: National Eat Your Vegetables Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to finally giving the neglected broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts on your plate the attention they deserve. Parents everywhere rejoice while kids negotiate for just two more bites.
holidays.origin: Like many unofficial food holidays, it grew out of grassroots nutrition and food-calendar traditions, popularized by health advocates and online holiday listings as a cheerful nudge to eat more produce.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'eat your vegetables' has been a parenting staple for generations, and a 1990 poll made broccoli famous when President George H. W. Bush declared he hated it.

holidays.name: World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that raises awareness about land degradation, drought, and how we can keep soil healthy. It is less about sand dunes taking over your backyard and more about protecting the ground that grows our food.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly proclaimed it in 1994 after the adoption of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, and it has been observed every June 17 since 1995.
holidays.funFact: Up to 40 percent of the world's land is estimated to be degraded, which affects roughly half of humanity.

holidays.name: Eat All Your Veggies Day
holidays.description: The cousin of Eat Your Vegetables Day, this one raises the stakes: no leaving the peas hiding under the mashed potatoes. A full plate cleared means you win the day.
holidays.origin: This is a modern internet-era observance with no single known founder, spread through social media and food-holiday calendars as a playful challenge to clean your plate of greens.
holidays.funFact: Carrots were originally purple, yellow, or white; the familiar orange variety was popularized by Dutch growers in the 1600s.

holidays.name: Juneteenth Eve and Iceland National Day Celebrations
holidays.description: Iceland celebrates its National Day with parades, flags, brass bands, and lots of ice cream even if the weather is chilly. Locals dress up, kids wave tiny flags, and the whole country throws a party for independence.
holidays.origin: Iceland's National Day marks the birthday of independence leader Jón Sigurðsson, born June 17, 1811, and the founding of the Republic of Iceland on June 17, 1944.
holidays.funFact: Icelanders famously love eating ice cream in cold weather, so the national celebration often features people licking cones in jackets.

holidays.name: Stupid Guy Thing Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek unofficial holiday that playfully celebrates the goofy, questionable decisions people make, like jumping off the roof into a pool or microwaving something that really should not be microwaved.
holidays.origin: It is a humorous unofficial observance that circulates on quirky holiday calendars, with no formal organization behind it, just people laughing at themselves.
holidays.funFact: The Darwin Awards, which humorously honor people who remove themselves from the gene pool through foolish acts, were launched in the early 1990s and became an internet phenomenon.
